To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glucose substrate cycle in the liver of normal dogs is small (about 13% of the rate of appearance, i.e., the rate of hepatic glucose output) but that it can be greatly enhanced by methylprednisolene treatment, exercise, and glucagon.
glucocorticoids (GCs), which are known to induce hyperglycemia in humans and animals, increase the rate of hepatic glucose production (HGP).

the hepatic glucose substrate cycle (SC) is a significant pathway of glucose production in normal and glucocorticoid-treated dogs, and that the glucocorticoids increase SC by elevating the activity of the multifunctional enzyme, glucokinase-glucose-6-phosphate phosphatase (gl-6-Pase), which catalyzes a reaction of the SC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
hepatic glucose metabolism in the normal state and in the glucocorticosteroid-induced state of hyperglycemia.
the regulation of the hepatic glucose cycle, and the results indicate that the glucocorticoids play a key role in this process.
the role of the liver in the regulation of the glucose cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
glucocorticoids increase the rate of glucose output from the liver by increasing the rate of glucose formation (gl-6-Pase), and the increase in SC represents the futile cycle of glucose.
the substrate cycle of glucose is an important component of hepatic glucose output and that glucocorticoid treatment greatly enhances its magnitude.

the substrate cycle of glucose is an important component of the hepatic glucose cycle and can be greatly increased by MP and glucagon, and that the glucocorticoids can increase hepatic glucose output by increasing both the recycling of carbon and the substrate cycle of hexoses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the glucose cycle in the liver is a dynamic process, and the glucocorticoids are potent modulators.
the glucocorticoids, by stimulating the activity of the multifunctional gl-6-Pases, increase the rate of glucose cycling and, therefore, the glucose turnover.
glucocorticoid increases the activity of the glucose cycle by elevating gl-6-P and by potentiating the multifunctional role of gl-6-phosphatase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the substrate cycle is a major determinant of glucose output in the glucocorticoidal condition and is not a mere artifact of the experimental approach.
glucocorticoids can greatly potentiate the glucose substrate cycle by increasing the activity of the multifunctional enzyme gl-6-P-ase.

the glucocorticoids greatly potentiate the substrate glucose cycle by increasing the activity of gl-6-phosphatase and that this cycle may play an important role in the pathogenesis of steroid diabetes.
